findings.evidence: Frontmatter has only name, permissionMode, tools and model. There is no description field.
findings.fix: Add: description: Write, run and fix pytest tests for a Python repository. Use when the user asks to add unit, integration, API, CLI, database, auth, billing, search, upload, export, email, cache, queue or payment tests, or to diagnose a failing test. Not for non-Python projects or for feature work with no testing component.
Remove permissionMode. A plugin agent ignores it, and bypassing permissions is unsafe for an agent that can edit and delete tests.

findings.evidence: "A unit test is a small piece of code that checks that another piece of code works... Mocking replaces a dependency with a fake one." The next section, "How to write a test in pytest", is a basic tutorial (create test_something.py, use assert, run pytest).
findings.fix: Delete the Background and pytest tutorial sections. The model already knows them. Keep only project-specific conventions.

findings.evidence: Fourteen identical sections from "### unit tests" to "### payment tests" differ only in the category word. Each has a placeholder example such as `run_unit_case()` and the line "Repeat the arrange, act and assert pattern...".
findings.fix: Replace them with one rule: name tests `test_<category>_<behavior>` and put them in `tests/<category>/`. Add one real example. Drop the boilerplate.

findings.evidence: The Instructions section is generic: "Be careful, think about edge cases and write good tests." It has no domain procedure or expert reasoning.
findings.fix: Write an ordered workflow: reproduce the failure, find the root cause, fix, run the affected tests, then run the wider suite. Add guidance on when a test is wrong and when the code is wrong.

findings.evidence: "Be careful, think about edge cases..." and "Do your best and make sure everything works." There is no specific NEVER list or gotcha with a reason.
findings.fix: Add a NEVER list with reasons. Examples: never delete or skip a failing test to get a green run, because that hides a real regression. Never weaken an assertion to match buggy output.

findings.evidence: The file is about 230 lines. About 195 of them are the repeated naming sections, with nothing split out and no skills: preload.
findings.fix: Collapse the naming reference into a short table or one rule. Or move it to a skill preloaded through `skills:`. This brings the file well under 200 lines.

findings.evidence: "Fix the code or the test, whichever is easier. Delete tests that get in the way." The agent has Bash, Edit and Write tools. permissionMode is bypassPermissions.
findings.fix: Require a reason before changing or deleting a test. Never delete tests that fail. Give exact commands for running tests. Remove the bypassPermissions setting.

findings.evidence: The body has no sentence saying when the task is done. It also gives no output format for the final report.
findings.fix: Add: "Done when the changed test files pass and the full suite shows no new failures. Report the files changed, the commands run and their pass/fail counts, in a short list."

findings.evidence: Step 1 says "Always run the whole test suite before you change anything." Step 2 (line 26) says "Never run the whole test suite, because it is slow". The two steps directly contradict each other.
findings.fix: Pick one rule. For example, run only the affected test file first, and run the full suite once before finishing. Give the reason.

findings.evidence: "If a test fails, follow the steps in the section 'Recovery' and then go on to step 12." There is no Recovery section, and the list ends at step 6.
findings.fix: Write a real failure-handling section: read the failure, decide whether the test or the code is wrong, fix it, re-run, and stop and report if it still fails after N attempts. Point to a step number that exists.
